title: Adequate affinization of a closed substack over its closed image
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $\phi:\mathcal X\to Y$ be an adequate moduli space [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space], and let $i:\mathcal Z\hookrightarrow\mathcal X$ be an algebraic closed substack, meaning a closed immersion as in [lem-sfb-stack-closed-immersion-calculus]. Here $Y$ is an algebraic space over $k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Write $j=\phi\circ i$ and $\mathcal B=j_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}$, using [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Then $\mathcal B$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-algebra. Write $E=\operatorname{Spec}_Y\mathcal B$ for its relative spectrum [lem-sfb-space-relative-spec-correspondence], and let $W\hookrightarrow Y$ be the closed subspace cut out by the quasi-coherent ideal $\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal B)$; equivalently $W$ is the scheme-theoretic image of $j$. The canonical morphisms give a factorization $j:\mathcal Z\xrightarrow{b}E\xrightarrow{e}W\hookrightarrow Y$ in which $b$ is an adequate moduli space. The morphism $e$ is a universal homeomorphism: for every algebraic-space morphism $W'\to W$, the map $|E\times_WW'|\to|W'|$ is a homeomorphism, with point spaces as in [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets]. No reducedness, finite-type, Noetherian or finite-inertia assumption is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 5.2.11, printed p.510, closed-substack specialization; Definition 3.3.1 for the underlying universal homeomorphism; published primary PDF read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-disjoint-closed-substacks-algebra-quotient] to $\mathcal Z$ and the empty closed substack. The second algebra is the zero algebra, so the product is $\mathcal A=i_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}$ and the result gives a quasi-coherent quotient $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal A$. On a scheme chart the closed immersion is $\operatorname{Spec}(D/J)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}D$, and its algebra is $D/J$; hence the defining functor of relative spectrum identifies $\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathcal X}\mathcal A$ with $\mathcal Z$. Apply [lem-sfb-adequate-relative-spectrum] to $\mathcal A$: its pushforward is quasi-coherent and its canonical relative-spectrum map is adequate. On every etale scheme $U\to Y$, the section convention in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra] identifies $\Gamma(\mathcal X_U,\mathcal A)$ with $\Gamma(\mathcal Z_U,\mathcal O)$, by the explicit formula for $\mathcal A$ in the first citation. Thus $\phi_*\mathcal A=\mathcal B$ and the adequate map is the required $b:\mathcal Z\to E$. Its evaluation map gives $j$ after composition with $E\to Y$.

source.place: Lemma 5.2.11, first assertion and closed-substack specialization, printed p.510; published primary PDF read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus], the kernel $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal B)$ is quasi-coherent, and on $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to Y$ affine etale it is the kernel of $R\to B=\mathcal B(U)$. By [lem-sfb-space-closed-ideal-correspondence] it defines a closed subspace $W$ with algebra $\mathcal O_Y/\mathcal I$. The inclusion of this quotient into $\mathcal B$ gives $e:E\to W$ by [lem-sfb-space-relative-spec-correspondence]. Its composite with $W\hookrightarrow Y$ is the original structure map of $E$, since the corresponding algebra maps compose to $\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal B$. The quotient kills exactly the functions pulled back to zero on $\mathcal Z$: a factorization through any other closed subspace with ideal $\mathcal J$ forces $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal I$, by evaluating these pulled-back functions. Conversely the map through $E$ gives a factorization through $W$. This is the minimal closed-subspace factorization, so $W$ is the scheme-theoretic image.

source.place: Lemma 5.2.11, closed-image identification, printed p.510; published primary PDF read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Fix an affine etale $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to Y$, and put $\mathcal V=\mathcal X_U$ and $\mathcal A_U=\mathcal A|_{\mathcal V}$. The map $\mathcal V\to U$ is adequate by [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-etale-locality], and therefore $R=\Gamma(\mathcal V,\mathcal O)$ and $R\to B=\Gamma(\mathcal V,\mathcal A_U)$ is its restriction map. It is adequately affine by [lem-sfb-affine-target-adequacy-criterion], using the power-lifting clause of the preceding citation. For $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, the ring map $R\to P$ is flat directly from the definition [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]: a tensor with $P$, the free module on monomials, is the direct sum of copies of the given module; tensoring an injection is therefore coefficientwise injective. By [lem-sfb-stack-flat-scalar-sections], the quotient $\mathcal O\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal A_U$ remains a quasi-coherent quotient on $\mathcal V_P$, and its section rings identify with $P$ and $B\otimes_RP=B[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. By [lem-sfb-adequately-affine-affine-target-base-change], $\mathcal V_P\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ is adequately affine. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-target-adequacy-criterion] to this quotient: every polynomial in $B[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ has a positive power in the image of $R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. This works for every $n\geq0$.

source.place: Lemma 5.2.11, final assertion; polynomial test of Remark 3.2.2 and Proposition 3.3.5, printed pp.496,498,510; published primary PDF read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Write $I=\ker(R\to B)$ and $R_0=R/I$, so $R_0\hookrightarrow B$ is injective; by [lem-sfb-space-relative-spec-correspondence] applied to $\mathcal O_Y/\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal B$, $W_U=W\times_YU=\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ and $e$ restricts over it to $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R_0$. Step 3 implies the polynomial power-lifting hypothesis for $R_0\hookrightarrow B$: compose each polynomial lift with $R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow R_0[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. Apply [lem-sfb-polynomial-power-lifting-universal-homeomorphism]. For every $R_0$-algebra $C$ it gives a homeomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_{R_0}B)\to\operatorname{Spec}C$; by the base-change clause of [lem-sfb-space-relative-spec-correspondence] this is the base change of $e_U:E_U\to W_U$ along $\operatorname{Spec}C\to W_U$. Applying this to each summand, $|E_U\times_{W_U}V|\to|V|$ is a homeomorphism for every scheme $V\to W_U$ which is a disjoint union of affine schemes; in particular its fibres are singletons.

source.place: Lemma 5.2.11, final assertion; Proposition 3.3.5; stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 0DTQ (lemma-check-universal-homeomorphism-covering); published primary PDF read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Let $e_U:E_U\to W_U$ be as in step 4. Now let $\mathcal T\to W_U$ be any algebraic stack and $p:\mathcal T_E=E_U\times_{W_U}\mathcal T\to\mathcal T$; these fibre products are algebraic by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $V\to\mathcal T$ with $V$ a disjoint union of affine schemes; its base change $V_E=E_U\times_{W_U}V\to\mathcal T_E$ is a smooth surjective atlas, and $V_E\to V$ is the homeomorphism above. Put $R'=V\times_{\mathcal T}V$. By [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets], $|p|$ is continuous, $|V|\to|\mathcal T|$ and $|V_E|\to|\mathcal T_E|$ are open surjections defining the quotient topologies, the fibres of $|V|\to|\mathcal T|$ are the classes of the image of $|R'|$, and points of $2$-fibre products surject onto fibre products of point sets. Surjectivity of $|p|$: lift $\tau\in|\mathcal T|$ to $v\in|V|$ and take the point of $|V_E|$ over $v$. Injectivity: let $z_1,z_2\in|\mathcal T_E|$ lie over $\tau$, lift them to $e_1,e_2\in|V_E|$ over $v_1,v_2\in|V|$; some $r\in|R'|$ has $s(r)=v_1$, $t(r)=v_2$, and some point of $|E_U\times_{W_U}R'|$ lies over $r$. Its two images in $|V_E|$ lie over $v_1,v_2$, hence are $e_1,e_2$ because the fibres of $|V_E|\to|V|$ are singletons; the two composites $E_U\times_{W_U}R'\to\mathcal T_E$ are $2$-isomorphic, so $z_1=z_2$. Closedness: for closed $F\subseteq|\mathcal T_E|$ its inverse image in $|V_E|$ is closed, its image in $|V|$ is closed, and by bijectivity this image is the inverse image of $|p|(F)$, which is therefore closed. So $|p|$ is a continuous closed bijection, a homeomorphism: $e_U$ is a universal homeomorphism in the sense of [lem-sfb-stack-etale-local-qcqs-homeomorphism].

source.place: Lemma 5.2.11, final assertion; Proposition 3.3.5; stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 0DTQ (lemma-check-universal-homeomorphism-covering); published primary PDF read online at https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: By step 5, each $e_U$ is a universal homeomorphism. Finally the $W_U\to W$ form a jointly surjective etale family: they are the base changes of the affine etale cover of $Y$. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-etale-local-qcqs-homeomorphism] to descend the universal-homeomorphism property to $e$; its base change by every algebraic-space morphism $W'\to W$ gives the homeomorphism $|E\times_WW'|\to|W'|$ of the statement.
